# Contributor licence agreement

This agreement lets the project distribute your contribution under the
project's licence without asking again for every change. It does not transfer
ownership of your work.

## Agreement

By signing, you confirm that:

1. you are the author of the contribution, or you have the right to submit it
   on behalf of its author;
2. you grant the project a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free,
   irrevocable licence to reproduce, modify, distribute, and sublicense the
   contribution under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3 or a
   later version; and
3. you are not aware of any claim that the contribution infringes someone
   else's rights.

You keep the copyright in your contribution. The project will identify the
human contributor in commits, the changelog, and release notes. It will not add
a tool, bot, or assistant as a contributor.

## Signing

A pull request from a first-time contributor needs a record in the
`cla-signatures` branch. A maintainer records the signature after the
contributor confirms the agreement in the pull request. The branch contains one
file per signing account, named with the account's login. Existing signatures
remain valid for later contributions.

If you are contributing on behalf of an employer or another organisation, say
so in the pull request so the maintainer can confirm that you have authority to
sign. If you cannot agree to these terms, open an issue before sending code and
we will see whether a different arrangement is possible.

This document is not legal advice. Ask your own adviser if the licence grant
matters to your employment or to your organisation.
